item.description: Okowa won 183 votes in the General Assembly and 13 in the Security Council. She is a professor of public international law at Queen Mary University of London and has served on the UN’s International Law Commission since 2021.

item.title: BBC Africa: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
item.description: As South Africans vote in local elections, residents tell the BBC they are tired of the poor quality of services they get.

item.title: BBC Africa: Rwanda's army team removed from Africa league after US sanctions, NBA says
item.description: The US imposed sanctions on Rwanda's army over its role in the conflict in DR Congo.

item.title: Africanews: Niger signs cooperation deal with military leader in eastern Libya
item.description: The agreement to expand cooperation in “various fields” was approved by Nigerien Prime Minister Ali Maha-man Lamine Zeine during a visit to Benghazi.

item.title: Africanews: Portugal: Housing protesters return to Lisbon square after court ruling
item.description: Housing protesters have returned to Lisbon's historic Rossio Square, setting up around 100 tents following a court ruling. The demonstration comes as Portugal's government faces growing pressure over housing.

item.title: Africanews: Haitian PM thanks El Salvador for support in fight against gangs
item.description: El Salvador sent more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti, the government said Wednesday, to support a mission to rescue four soldiers serving in a UN-backed force missing after an ambush.

item.title: Africanews: Ukraine: 33 dead, over 50 missing after Russian bombing in Zaporizhzhia
item.description: Russian strikes on a humanitarian aid site in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region have killed 33 people, with more than 50 still missing, on Monday 2 November. Survivors and rescuers are being treated for severe injuries.

item.title: Africanews: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms becomes first Black woman governor in US history
item.description: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, a former Atlanta mayor, won the race for governor in the southern state of Georgia on Tuesday, making her the first Black woman elected to the top office in any US state, media projections showed.

item.title: Africanews: US midterm elections: Cheers erupt as Talarico's Texas victory is projected
item.description: Supporters erupted in celebration in Austin as Democrat James Talarico was projected to win a US Senate seat in Texas, a state where his party has not won a Senate election since 1988.

item.title: Africanews: Democrats seize Congress as Trump refuses to take blame
item.description: President Donald Trump had rare praise for rival Democrats Tuesday after their stunning US midterm elections victory and admitted the Iran war may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party.

item.title: Africanews: South Africans vote amid growing discontent over failing services and infrastructure
item.description: South Africans head to the polls on Wednesday for local government elections, with voters set to choose their municipal representatives amid growing concerns over unemployment, crime, water shortages and the delivery of basic services.

item.title: Africanews: US requires air passengers to attest they haven’t visited Ebola-hit DRC
item.description: US-bound air passengers must sign a statement that they have not travelled to the Democratic Republic of Congo, the epicentre of a deadly Ebola outbreak, under new rules coming into force on Tuesday, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

item.title: Africanews: UN peacekeeping head meets leaders of rebel coalition in eastern DRC
item.description: The head of the UN’s MONUSCO peacekeeping mission to Congo met with the DRC’s former president Joseph Kabila on Tuesday and other leaders of his new coalition.

item.title: Africanews: King Charles addresses 'monstrous injustice' of slavery as UK PM mulls apology
item.description: The transatlantic slave trade was a ‘monstrous injustice,’ Britain’s King Charles III said on Tuesday in a speech to Commonwealth leaders. But he stopped short of an apology.

item.title: Africanews: Disruptions to basic services loom over South Africa's local polls
item.description: As voters in Johannesburg ready for Wednesday’s local elections, basic services are top of their concerns. South Africa’s economic capital and largest city, Johannesburg has seen nearly two weeks of disruption to its water supply, with severe outages and low pressure in parts of the city.

item.title: Africanews: Senegalese lawmakers reject key budget in major setback for IMF talks
item.description: Dakar is hoping to secure a $2.2 billion three-year IMF bailout programme aimed at stabilising its public finances.

item.title: Africanews: Tenerife footballer Jesús De Miguel dies aged 30 after match collision
item.description: The Spanish player had a cardiac arrest after he was struck in the chest when challenging the ball.

item.title: Africanews: South Africa's first bread sommelier perfects centuries-old tradition
item.description: A centuries-old Cape Winelands tradition is now on the global culinary map. Mosbolletjies is a traditional brioche made with grape must. Now a recipe for the bread created by a South African baker has won him the title of Bread Sommelier.

item.title: Africanews: Pix of the Day, 3rd November, 2026 - Across the world
item.description: Pix of the Day, 3rd November, 2026 - Across the world

item.title: Africanews: Egypt: 104th anniversary of the discovery of King Tutankhamun's tomb
item.description: The unearthing of his 3,000 year-old tomb and all its treasures is seen as one of the greatest archaeological discoveries of all time.

item.title: Africanews: Americans vote in midterm election that could upend Trump presidency
item.description: Voters across the United States are going to the polls on Tuesday and Washington is bracing for a major upheaval. President Trump’s Republican Party currently holds both chambers of Congress. But poll watchers are predicting a Democratic wave that could see that all change.

item.title: Africanews: What Europe can learn from Africa’s mobile banking success
item.description: Africa is no longer simply a continent catching up with the rest of the world. In mobile banking, product simplicity and the ability to combine tradition with technology, it is ahead of many markets considered developed, Marta Mróz-Sipiora of Asseco Poland tells Euronews.

item.title: Africanews: Dakar mash-up combines Swiss and Senegalese wrestling traditions
item.description: Dakar mash-up combines Swiss and Senegalese wrestling traditions on the sidelines of the 2026 Youth Olympic Games.

item.title: Africanews: ICC president hits back at Trump administration penalties
item.description: The president of the International Criminal Court accused the Trump administration of trying to obstruct international justice by imposing penalties on the tribunal and vowed that it would not succeed.

item.title: Africanews: Ethiopia's Tigray rebels claim to have inflicted heavy losses on army
item.description: It says it killed 500 soldiers and wounded 800 others during a counteroffensive near the historic town of Aksum on Saturday.
